gaps.sentence: She apologized for the ___ caused by the delay (CONVENIENT).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — the delay was a bad thing
gaps.explanation: A delay causes inconvenience (negative prefix in- + noun); the sentence needs the noun, not the adjectives.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: There has been a big ___ (IMPROVE) in her tennis.
gaps.explanation: After 'a big' a noun is needed: improvement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: The crowd waited ___ for the gates to open (PATIENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'waited': patiently. 'Patients' are people in hospital.

gaps.sentence: She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.

gaps.sentence: His sudden ___ came as a shock to everyone (DEPART).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject (-ure); beware the word meaning 'part of an organisation'
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'depart' is departure (-ure); a department is a section of an organisation.

gaps.sentence: We must ___ our efforts to finish on time (STRONG).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: strengthen. A base verb follows 'must'.
